attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The quoted Information passage nearby is separate and not used.

semantics.note: The wording is firm ('will', 'can't actually support'), so this is a scored forecast. The normalised proposition keeps the commissioning setting and the market-wide scope. 'Eventually' means there is no deadline.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: a market-wide shortfall in paying demand as the pipeline opens, not the failure of every facility. Treating 18-36 months as build time rather than a deadline matches the text. Requiring actual payments rather than preleases is reasonable.

evidence.note: CBRE H1 2026 data (available before the evaluation date) shows record-low vacancy and 80.4% preleasing. It covers the broader market before the forecast cohort opens and measures commitments, not sustained payments. Material, but context only.
Moody's says completion is not the same as cash flow and points to power constraints. It neither shows nor rules out a market-wide shortage of paying customers.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has no post-commissioning data on occupancy, paid use or collections for the publication-date pipeline. CBRE's strong preleasing and low vacancy come from before the forecast window and are not proof of sustained paying demand. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the claim stays unresolved.
